title: Saṅkalpa for the arghya (evening)

words.meaning: the offering of the arghya of the sandhyā

samasa.meaning: the giving of the arghya (water of honour) of the sandhyā

translation.literal: I shall perform the giving of the evening sandhyā’s arghya.
translation.readable: I shall offer the arghya of the evening Sandhyā.

meaning: The saṅkalpa, the statement of intent, for the arghya in the evening. The witness prints the opening of the saṅkalpa (mamopātta … prītyartham, ‘by way of destroying all the faults I have incurred, for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord’) once, and then only this closing part for each time of day; the opening is said before it. The verbs are first person: the worshipper speaks for himself, and the formula is the same for every performer.

notes.label: traditional
notes.text: A saṅkalpa is said with the breath held after the prāṇāyāma, or immediately after it; it names the act, the time, and the purpose. The Smārta form offers the act for the pleasure of the Supreme Lord (Parameśvara); Vaiṣṇava prayogas use other wording, which is outside this edition.
